thread.title: Twitter Chart Is a “Technical Goldmine,” Shares Could Jump 20%: Trader

author: investopedia.com
title: Twitter Chart Is a “Technical Goldmine,” Shares Could Jump 20%: Trader
text:
Shares of Twitter Inc. ( TWTR ), which have struggled to keep up with the rest of the tech industry over the recent years, are now outperforming the broader market during a rocky time for once high flying tech companies. With shares of the social media giant already up about 15% over the recent one-month period and nearly 60% YTD, one market watcher is forecasting bigger gains ahead.
'Beautiful Cup and Handle' Positions Twitter Stock for Breakout In an interview with CNBC's "Trading Nation" on Wednesday, Bill Baruch, the president of Blue Line Futures, highlighted Twitter as a bright spot in the struggling tech sector, as major players such as Amazon.com Inc. ( AMZN ), Facebook Inc. ( FB ) and Apple Inc. ( AAPL ) remain either in or on the brink of, bear market territory.
Baruch called Twitter's stock a "technical goldmine," indicating that the stock's charts are signaling an even larger rally ahead. In September, the strategist called for a bottom in Twitter's sell-off at $27. On Oct. 11, shares fell to $26.19, found support and then surged 25% to current levels.
"It's forming a beautiful cup and handle. I think the technicals are really continuing here and the cup and handle lays the groundwork out that we're going to break out," said Baruch. In such a scenario, which is viewed as a bullish indicator, a stock pulls back and then returns to the beginning of a formation's peak, forming a "cup". The stock then experiences a short period of losses, which creates a "handle."
"The resistance is still the 100-day moving average, the 200-day moving average, those are November highs. But if we get above there, you're going to see a tailwind up to near $40 and probably exceeding $40," he said.
A move to $40 reflects a more than 21% upside from Thursday close, with Twitter stock down 0.5% at $32.98.
Michael Bapis, managing director of Vois Advisors at Rockefeller Capital Management, chimed in on the CNBC segment with a similarly upbeat outlook, arguing that Twitter's widespread use, "from the president to CEOs and athletes," should support its future growth.
